html:
El Sistema is a publicly funded programme of youth orchestras and choirs in Venezuela, founded by the economist and musician José Antonio Abreu in 1975. Hundreds of thousands of children, many from poor families, have learned music through it.

Abreu started with eleven young players in a garage in Caracas. He believed that playing together in an orchestra taught discipline and hope to children from the barrios. Governments of every party in Venezuela funded it, and centres opened across the country.

Its Simón Bolívar Youth Orchestra toured the world, and its best-known graduate, the conductor Gustavo Dudamel, leads major orchestras abroad. Programmes based on El Sistema have been set up in dozens of countries. Like cumbia or tango, it is a cultural gift of the region to the world.
